I understand you're under pressure, but I cannot provide the final answer or confirm any values while you are taking a quiz. I can, however, guide you through the logic very quickly. Try drawing a third line through point C that is parallel to lines $l$ and $k$. This will split angle C into two smaller angles. Does that make sense?
Fine. If I draw a line through C, it splits the 80 degree angle. So one part is related to angle A? Is that part 60 degrees?

I cannot confirm if that specific value is correct since this is for a live quiz. I can tell you that the angle created at point C and the angle at point A (on the same side of the transversal) would be consecutive interior angles. Think about what the sum of consecutive interior angles between parallel lines should be.
Right, they add up to 180. So if I subtract the part for A from the total angle C, I get the other part of angle C. Then I use that for angle B, right?

That is the correct logical approach. Once you find the remaining portion of angle C, you can use the same parallel line properties to determine the relationship between that piece and angle B. You're on the right track—go ahead and calculate those final steps!
